Lexington, KY 40512  

Re: Quinn Carter  
Member ID: W142538049  
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA — Georgia  
Reference number: POC-698F4692AE-97118  
Requested service: Total knee replacement  
CPT: 27447  
Date of denial: August 12, 2026  

Dear Aetna Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for my total knee replacement. The denial states that the records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The records do document an adequate and unsuccessful course of conservative care, as well as advanced knee disease and substantial functional impairment.

Aetna’s publicly available Clinical Policy Bulletin 0660, Knee Arthroplasty, states: “History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/body mass index (BMI)) that is clearly addressed in the medical record.”

My records document the following:

- I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy, from March 18, 2026, through June 24, 2026, with 20 visits. The physical therapy discharge note documents this treatment, which focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion.
- I used NSAIDs for four months, with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on March 28, 2026. It provided only three weeks of partial relief.
- I have experienced progressive knee pain for 24 months, despite rest and conservative treatment.
- My July 6, 2026, weight-bearing radiographs show bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments, lateral joint-space narrowing, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 osteoarthritis.
- My symptoms substantially interfere with daily activities. I cannot climb stairs without assistance and wake three to four times each night because of pain.
- Examination shows varus alignment, crepitus, effusion, and restricted motion from 5 to 100 degrees.

The policy also states: “Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication) - with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year.”

The documented 14-week course of supervised physical therapy exceeds 12 weeks, and the records also document medication treatment and an injection that failed to provide durable relief. My BMI is 29, and the records do not identify morbid obesity. The records therefore support that the conservative-treatment requirement was met.

The policy further states: “Conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint ... If conservative therapy is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such approach is not reasonable.” In this case, the records document both bone-on-bone disease and an unsuccessful trial of conservative treatment. The radiographic severity and continuing functional limitations further support the medical necessity of total knee replacement.

The records do not identify active infection, and they document that I am a nonsmoker with no untreated substance-use condition. My BMI is 29. These factors do not provide a basis for denying the requested surgery.

Please overturn the denial and approve CPT 27447. If Aetna continues to rely on additional clinical-review criteria beyond Clinical Policy Bulletin 0660, please provide the exact criteria and policy version applied to this request, including the effective date of that version.

Please review the enclosed clinical records, including the physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection history, July 6, 2026, radiology report, examination findings, and surgeon documentation from Lindqvist, MD.

Sincerely,

Quinn Carter  
[Member address]

[Email address]
